messages.subject: split out derived data
parts:
Motivated by Ben's example from Wawro,
I committed changes to split out derived data
from derived parameters and give both their own
statement(s).

Splitting out derived data and its computation
is more efficient than using derived parameters.
I think it's also clearer as to what's going on.

Derived data variables generate class member variables
for the model and the statement(s) get generated
at the end of the constructor (so they only get
executed once).

I renamed the "derived" block, which was implicitly
parameters before, to "derived parameters". I also
allowed statements to be added as for data. Unlike
for data, these go at the start of the log prob,
so they don't behave any differently than statmeents
inside the model.

Here's a model that illustrates the new
syntax (though it's not good on motivation).

------------------------------
data {
double mu;
double(0,) sigma;
}
derived data {
double mu_pp;

mu_pp <- mu + 1;
mu_pp <- 2 * mu_pp;
}
parameters {
double y;
}
derived parameters {
double z;
double w[1];

z <- y * 2.0 + 1.0;
w[0] <- pow(z,3.0);
}
model {
y ~ normal(mu,sigma);
}
----------------------------------

- Bob
